dependent_variable.definition: For the selected Table 2 model, decision quality is an indicator for whether the participant chose the winning model in their own factory (Alpha) on a choice. Table 2 defines the indicator as 1 for choosing the winner and 0 otherwise; Appendix A reports a conflicting ±0.5 coding.

independent_variables.name: LowContr
independent_variables.definition: Randomly assigned compensation-measure condition, representing accountability for uncontrollable outcomes. Participants in the more-controllable condition receive pay based only on their own factory’s outcomes; in the less-controllable condition, pay is based 50% on their own factory and 50% on the two uncontrollable factories.
independent_variables.formula: −0.5 for the more-controllable condition; +0.5 for the less-controllable condition.

In the condition with the more controllable measure, participants are paid based only on the outcomes in their own factory.
In the condition with the less controllable measure, participants are paid based 50% on the outcomes in their own factory and 50% on the outcomes in the two uncontrollable factories

review_notes: Appendix A (physical page 30) says DecQual equals 0.5 for a correct choice and −0.5 otherwise. The selected main-results table note (physical page 22) says DecQual equals 1 for a correct choice and 0 otherwise. The model definition follows the table note for the selected regression; the paper’s conflicting coding statement remains flagged for review.

The principal baseline is H1: Table 2 column 1 includes the ChoiceNum fixed effects and tests the average effect of LowContr. Column 2 is the same H1 test without those fixed effects. Columns 3–5 test the separate H2/H3 moderators, which the paper calls stress tests; subsequent learning and attention analyses are outside this baseline family.

results_review_notes: Table 1 reports the DecQual participant-level mean, SD, and N separately for the two LowContr conditions; it has no LowContr descriptive row.
The DecQual coding conflict between the main-results note and Appendix A is carried through to descriptive review status.
